Bail Bond Information for Matanuska-Susitna County

After booking into Matanuska-Susitna County jail, a judge typically sets bail at arraignment (often within 24–72 hours). Families often work with a licensed bail bondsman. A common commercial bond fee is about 10% of the bail amount (non-refundable). Example: $10,000 bail → roughly $1,000 premium, subject to local rules.

If the person cannot afford bail, they may request a reduction hearing or public defender.

For hearing schedules, contact the Matanuska-Susitna County court.

What to Expect After Arrest in Matanuska-Susitna County

Typical steps after arrest in Matanuska-Susitna County:

  1. Booking — fingerprints, photo, property inventory
  2. Medical screening — before general population housing
  3. Classification — housing based on charges and history
  4. Arraignment — first court appearance; bail often set here
  5. Transfer — serious cases may move to a state facility

Frequently Asked Questions — Matanuska-Susitna County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in Matanuska-Susitna County jail?

Start with the official Matanuska-Susitna County inmate roster. You can also call Alaska Department of Corrections at (907) 745-0200. Online records often lag booking by a few hours.

What is the phone number for Mat-Su Pretrial Facility?

Contact Alaska Department of Corrections at (907) 745-0200. Facility address on file: 1210 N. Bruce Drive, Palmer, AK 99645.

How long does booking take in Matanuska-Susitna County?

Booking commonly takes 2–8 hours depending on volume at Mat-Su Pretrial Facility. Weekends and holidays can delay when a name appears in any published system. If urgent, call the facility directly rather than waiting on a website refresh.

Can I visit an inmate at Matanuska-Susitna County jail?

Usually yes if the person is eligible and the facility is accepting visits. The main facility listed is Mat-Su Pretrial Facility at 1210 N. Bruce Drive, Palmer, AK 99645. Bring government photo ID and confirm hours and dress code with Alaska Department of Corrections before you go. Video visitation may be offered.

What if the person is not listed in the county system?

They may have been released, transferred, or booked under a different name spelling. Check Alaska Department of Corrections and the Federal BOP locator for federal custody. Then call Alaska Department of Corrections to confirm.

How do I send money to someone at Mat-Su Pretrial Facility?

Ask Mat-Su Pretrial Facility which commissary vendor they use (often JPay, Securus, or Access Corrections) when you call (907) 745-0200. Limits and fees vary by facility — confirm before sending money.
